title: Split the new-pane button into New Terminal and New Claude
notes:
The title row's '+ New pane' becomes two halves: [New Terminal | New Claude]. New Terminal is today's button and the terminal-add key. New Claude opens a new worker pane and starts the claude command in its shell, in the project's folder.

Keyboard first: New Claude gets its own key, a row in src/shared/keys/actions.ts beside terminal-add (a terminals-scope name), and src/renderer/keys/help.ts plus the terminals blurb say so. Both halves keep the button's mousedown preventDefault, so a click leaves the keyboard where it was; the new pane takes it once it opens, as addPane does now.

Why the claude command and not a Claude screen (pane run --screen): the terminal Claude is full Claude Code, comes back after a restart through the pane host, and needs no new session plumbing. A Claude screen opened by hand would start empty, and screen parity is a backlog card of its own (a6b5043b).

A Claude opened this way is the user's, not main's worker: it reports to nobody when its turn ends (workers README, 'a Claude opened by hand tells nobody').

Checks: the decision of which command a new pane starts with goes in a small module with a test (workflow-rule-2); docs/panes README and history get a line.
